# Software architecture and microservices examples

These Java and Spring examples explore how the same catalogue and cart domain
can evolve from a layered monolith to a distributed system. Compare the
boundaries, communication, deployment and operational trade-offs of each style;
the examples are teaching material, not production blueprints.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)
- A container runtime for exercises that run infrastructure or containers.
  Some exercises specifically require Docker or Docker-compatible test support.
- Network access to download Maven dependencies and, where applicable,
  container images.

Check each example’s runbook for its specific tools, services, ports and cleanup
instructions.

## Examples

The completed examples can be used independently. The following order follows
the workshop narrative:

1. [Layered monolith](./application-monolithic-layered-single-project/README.md):
   Start with a single application organised into technical layers.
2. [Modular monolith in a single project](./application-monolithic-modular-single-project/README.md):
   Introduce domain boundaries within one deployable application.
3. [Multi-project modular monolith](./application-monolithic-modular-multi-project/README.md):
   Express module boundaries as separate projects while retaining a monolithic
   deployment.
4. [Synchronous REST services](./application-distributed-rest-synchronous/README.md):
   Split the application into services and explore synchronous communication and
   distributed observability.
5. [Cascading failure](./application-distributed-rest-cascading-failure/README.md):
   Explore a failure scenario that extends the synchronous services discussion.
6. [Asynchronous messaging](./application-distributed-messaging-queue-asynchronous/README.md):
   Communicate through a message queue and explore the consequences of
   asynchronous coordination.

The [guided refactoring flow](./refactoring/) provides a separate, experimental
step-by-step route through the architecture changes, including observability.
Each example includes its own architectural decision records.

Use the workshop’s DORA and SPACE discussion to consider potential delivery and
team impacts; these examples alone do not measure those outcomes.

## Common commands

Run these commands from the `examples` directory. Building all projects may run
tests that require container infrastructure; consult the individual runbooks
before running them.

Build the Maven reactor:

```shell
./mvnw clean package -DskipTests
```

Tests are skipped when building all projects because some require external
services that may not be running. Run the tests separately, following each
example’s setup instructions.

Run tests for the layered monolith:

```shell
./mvnw test --projects application-monolithic-layered-single-project
```
